core: What sales is: the activities that convert a customer's interest into a purchase (working definition from OpenStax's personal-selling material)
The selling process: prospecting, approaching, presenting, handling objections, closing, follow-up
Sales versus marketing: individual deals versus market-wide attraction
Sales channels: in-person, phone, and online selling
Relationships in sales: trust, follow-up, and repeat business
The honest framing: sales as listening and solving, not pushing
supporting: Personal selling's place in the promotional mix (face-to-face presentation)
Objection handling as a normal part of moving a sale forward
How businesses combine multiple sales channels in one purchase
outOfScope: Marketing strategy and the four Ps (sibling topic: marketing)
Advertising and promotion-mix depth (owned by the marketing topic)

claims.claim: Sales is the business activity that converts a customer's interest into a purchase; the working definition used in this lesson — sales incorporates actually selling the company's products or services to its customers — comes from OpenStax's material on personal selling.
The selling process has six steps: prospecting and qualifying, approaching, presenting, handling objections, closing, and follow-up.
Handling objections means addressing the customer's concerns rather than ignoring them; it is a normal part of moving a sale forward.
Marketing attracts interest and communicates value so that a product sells, while sales actually sells the product to customers; the two jobs work together.
Sales channels include face-to-face (in-person) selling, telephone selling (including telemarketing), and online selling, and many businesses combine channels in one purchase.
Follow-up after the sale confirms customer satisfaction and is the source of repeat business.
Sales targets (quotas) are minimum goals a salesperson must meet over a set period, measured by value, volume, or activity.
Effective selling rests on listening and solving the customer's problem rather than pushing; trust drives repeat business.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Textbooks and companies name the steps of the selling process differently (step counts vary, and steps are renamed or merged).
positions: OpenStax uses six steps: prospecting/qualifying, approaching, presenting, handling objections, closing, follow-up
Other sources compress steps (for example, folding qualifying into prospecting) or expand them (for example, adding preparation before the approach)
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson uses OpenStax's six-step process as its naming and notes that companies adapt the names while keeping the same overall shape.

sourceRecords.title: Introduction to Business, Section 12.7: The Importance of Personal Selling
sourceRecords.notes: Tier A open textbook. openstax.org blocks direct fetching, so the section was read via an Internet Archive capture of this URL on 2026-08-21. Confirms the personal-selling material behind the working definition of sales, the six-step selling process (prospecting/qualifying, approaching, presenting, handling objections, closing, follow-up), the rationale for handling objections, and the follow-up/repeat-sales point. Concepts adapted into original prose; no wording reproduced verbatim.
